subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw make source-channel visible output final-only/message-tool-only by default for tool-using turns, including direct chats and cron announce delivery, or preserve automatic bare-text replies with narrower suppression guards?
rationale: This choice trades security and professional-channel leakage prevention against backward compatibility for users who rely on automatic plain-text DM replies; code inspection shows both behaviors are currently intentional in different paths.

options.title: Adopt final-only/source-tool delivery with migration
options.body: Make tool-using source turns private unless the final answer or message tool explicitly delivers, and add upgrade-facing docs/tests or a transition knob for direct-chat compatibility.

options.title: Keep automatic replies, add narrow guards
options.body: Preserve current automatic defaults and patch only known commentary, reasoning, silent-final, and cron payload leak shapes, accepting more edge-case risk.

options.title: Land partial opt-ins first
options.body: Ship narrow opt-in mitigations such as final-tag enforcement or verbose-off suppression while leaving the default policy unresolved.

recommendation.title: Adopt final-only/source-tool delivery with migration
recommendation.body: Make tool-using source turns private unless the final answer or message tool explicitly delivers, and add upgrade-facing docs/tests or a transition knob for direct-chat compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue needs a maintainer-level security and compatibility decision around the delivery boundary that recent phase-separation merges route through this owner.
